display.purpose: The thrust figure only. 88px below 1240px wide, 84px on a phone.

headline.purpose: The engine's name in the top bar, in capitals. Efficiency (34px) and the Fire button's word (32px) sit in the same range.

title.purpose: Mid-sized figures and names: throttle and altitude readings, gauge percentages, nozzle state, engine names in the picker (19 to 21px).

body.purpose: Control names, dropdown text, buttons and sentences. Tabular figures on.

note.purpose: The Dim line of explanation under a part picker or a figure. The log and tooltips use 13.5px.

label.purpose: Uppercase Dim name of a reading, a control or a panel. Always names the thing beneath or beside it.

shadows.name: notice
shadows.purpose: The failure notice over the picture.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one easing curve (--ease): fast start, long settle. Chevron turn, Fire press, flash, log lines.

motion.name: control-state
motion.purpose: Border and fill change on a button's hover.

motion.name: fire-press
motion.purpose: The Fire button nudges down while pressed.

motion.name: ignition-flash
motion.purpose: A warm radial flash from the nozzle exit when the engine lights. Off for reduced motion.

motion.name: ignition-shudder
motion.purpose: The picture, the stand and the callouts shake together at ignition. Off for reduced motion.

motion.name: log-arrive
motion.purpose: A new test log line arriving. Off for reduced motion.

motion.name: forecast-fade
motion.purpose: Readings coming up from half strength as the engine lights.

components.name: Button
components.description: The ordinary control button. Hover brightens the border; switched on, border and lettering turn yellow.
components.css: .ds-btn-row { display: flex; gap: 8px; } .ds-btn { font: 15px/1.4 var(--body); color: var(--text); background: var(--panel-2); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 3px; padding: 6px 10px; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.15s, background-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--dim); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--yellow); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.45; cursor: default; } .ds-btn-on { border-color: var(--yellow); color: var(--yellow); }

components.name: Fire Button (armed)
components.description: The one red button, with its Armed label above. Sits on the picture's centreline.
components.css: .ds-firebox { display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 7px; width: 216px; } .ds-arm { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; font: 700 13px/1 var(--display); letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--yellow); } .ds-arm::before { content: ''; width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; } .ds-fire { width: 216px; min-height: 60px; padding: 10px 12px 11px; background: var(--red-fill); border: 1px solid var(--red-fill); border-radius: 3px; color: #fff; font: 700 32px/1 var(--display); letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.12s var(--ease), background-color 0.15s; } .ds-fire:hover { background: #b32218; border-color: #b32218; } .ds-fire:active { transform: translateY(2px); } .ds-fire:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--yellow); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Fire Button (firing)
components.description: While the engine runs the button inverts and reads Shut down.
components.css: .ds-firebox-f { display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 7px; width: 216px; } .ds-arm-f { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; font: 700 13px/1 var(--display); letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--red-text); } .ds-arm-f::before { content: ''; width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; } .ds-fire-f { width: 216px; min-height: 60px; padding: 10px 12px 11px; background: var(--well); border: 1px solid var(--red); border-radius: 3px; color: var(--red-text); font: 700 32px/1 var(--display); letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.12s var(--ease), background-color 0.15s; } .ds-fire-f:active { transform: translateY(2px); } .ds-fire-f:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--yellow); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Numbered Part Picker
components.description: A part picker in the Build column: a numbered ring that matches the mark on the engine, a dropdown and a one-line note.
components.css: .ds-part { display: block; width: 258px; font: 15px/1.4 var(--body); color: var(--text); } .ds-part-name { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 3px; } .ds-part-no { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 20px; height: 20px; border: 1px solid var(--text); border-radius: 50%; font: 700 13px/1 var(--display); } .ds-part:hover .ds-part-no, .ds-part:focus-within .ds-part-no { background: var(--yellow); border-color: var(--yellow); color: var(--ink); } .ds-select { width: 100%; font: inherit; color: var(--text); background: var(--panel-2); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 3px; padding: 6px 10px; } .ds-select:hover { border-color: var(--dim); } .ds-select:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--yellow); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-part-note { display: block; margin-top: 5px; color: var(--dim); font-size: 12.5px; line-height: 1.35; }

components.name: Callout
components.description: The numbered mark on the engine. Hover or focus turns it solid yellow; clicking goes to its picker.
components.css: .ds-callouts { display: flex; gap: 12px; padding: 8px; } .ds-callout { width: 24px; height: 24px; padding: 0; display: grid; place-items: center; background: var(--ink); color: var(--text); border: 1px solid var(--text); border-radius: 50%; font: 700 14px/1 var(--display); cursor: pointer; } .ds-callout:hover, .ds-callout-lit { background: var(--yellow); border-color: var(--yellow); color: var(--ink); } .ds-callout:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--yellow); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Slider
components.description: A thin scale with a flat block for a handle. Name and bold current value sit above.

components.name: Redline Gauges
components.description: A limit gauge ticked every tenth, with the redline from 85%. Green within limits, yellow in the redline, red past the limit.
components.html:
Wall stress60%
Heat load91%
Instability104%
components.css: .ds-gauges { display: grid; gap: 11px; width: 288px; color: var(--text); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-meter { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto; align-items: baseline; row-gap: 4px; } .ds-k { font: 700 13px/1.2 var(--display); letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--dim); } .ds-pct { font: 700 20px/1 var(--display); text-align: right; } .ds-bar { grid-column: 1 / -1; position: relative; height: 12px; background: var(--well); border-radius: 2px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-bar::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0 calc(10% - 1px), rgba(233, 236, 230, 0.28) calc(10% - 1px) 10%); } .ds-redline { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; right: 0; left: 85%; background: rgba(229, 55, 43, 0.4); border-left: 2px solid var(--red); } .ds-fill { position: relative; display: block; height: 100%; background: var(--green); } .ds-meter-amber .ds-fill { background: var(--yellow); } .ds-meter-amber .ds-pct { color: var(--yellow); } .ds-meter-red .ds-fill { background: var(--red); } .ds-meter-red .ds-pct { color: var(--red-text); }

components.name: Nozzle State Chip

narrative.overview:
The whole screen is one hot-fire test. The picture in the middle is the view of the engine on its stand, the column on the left is where the engine is built, the row under the picture is the console you fire it from, and the column on the right is the test data. Nothing is a "settings sidebar" or a "stat tile": every control changes the engine or the test, and every number is a reading from the physics.

The look is a working console, not a film prop. Surfaces are flat grey-green panels with thin dividing lines. There are no bezels, screws, glass, textures or toggle levers, and the controls are ordinary web controls (dropdowns, sliders, buttons, fold-open sections) so they behave the way everyone already expects. The character comes from the condensed engineering lettering, the very large thrust figure, the redline gauges and the timestamped test log.

Colour is kept for meaning. Almost everything is grey-green and off-white; red, yellow and green each have one job and appear nowhere else.
keyCharacteristics: One screen, three columns and a console row; on a desktop nothing scrolls as a page.
Three signal colours with one job each: red for fire and the redline, yellow for armed, attention and selection, green for within limits.
Flat panels, thin lines, small corners. No decoration.
Condensed bold capitals for figures and labels; a plain sans for sentences. Digits never jiggle as they change.
Numbered marks on the engine match numbered part pickers in the Build column.
Every reading says whether it is a forecast (engine cold) or live (engine lit).

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Red means fire or past the redline. Yellow means armed, look here, or selected. Green means within limits. If a new element does not mean one of those things, it is grey-green or off-white.

rules.name: The Three Reds Rule
rules.body: Red has three shades because it has three surfaces: `red-fill` under white lettering, `red-text` for red lettering on dark, `red` for lines and gauge fills. Do not use `red` for small text or as a button fill.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Figures, labels and names are Barlow Condensed 700 in capitals. Sentences are Barlow in ordinary case. Never write a sentence in condensed capitals, and never set a figure in the body face.

rules.name: The Steady Digits Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures are on for the whole page, so a number that changes many times a second does not shift sideways. Any element that shows a changing number must keep them on.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: If it is part of the console, it has no shadow. A soft dark shadow is only for something that opens over the console and closes again.

rules.name: The Solid Label Rule
rules.body: Labels on the picture (clock, view switch, zoom, notices) are the Well colour at 86 to 96% strength with a 1px border. They are nearly solid, never frosted or blurred.

rules.name: The Same Number Rule
rules.body: A number on the engine and a number in the Build column always mean the same part. Numbers are counted from the pickers that are showing, so they never skip.

rules.name: The Forecast Rule
rules.body: While the engine is unlit, every figure, gauge fill and the nozzle chip are shown at half strength and the chip's border is dashed. They come up to full strength as the engine lights, and the thrust figure counts up with it.

dos: Do follow the One Job Rule: red for fire and the redline, yellow for armed, attention and selection, green for within limits.
Do keep surfaces flat: a solid grey-green fill, a 1px Line border where needed, 3px corners.
Do set every figure, label and name in Barlow Condensed 700 capitals, and every sentence in Barlow.
Do keep tabular figures on wherever a number changes.
Do give every reading a Dim uppercase label that names it, and a plain-English line beneath when the figure needs explaining.
Do use the browser's own controls (select, range, button, details) and restyle them lightly.
Do show state with the border and lettering colour, not with a new fill.
Do say whether figures are a forecast or live, and show forecasts at half strength.
Do switch off the flash, the shake and any sliding for reduced motion.
Do use the colour variables on `:root` in `src/style.css` rather than typing a colour in.
donts: Don't use red, yellow or green as decoration, for a brand accent, or for an ordinary button.
Don't add bezels, screws, glass, brushed-metal textures, glows or toggle levers. It is a console, not a prop.
Don't put shadows on anything that is part of the console; shadows are for things that open over it.
Don't blur or frost anything. Labels on the picture are nearly solid.
Don't round corners beyond 3px, apart from the round numbered callouts and the status dot.
Don't separate things with cards or boxes inside a panel; use a label, spacing and a 1px line.
Don't add a third typeface or a third weight.
Don't use an uppercase label as decoration above a heading. A label names a reading, a control or a panel, and nothing else.
Don't show a figure that is not from the physics, or hide whether it was simulated or calculated.
